source_text: Verum demiror ubique constantiam disputantis, qui pronuntiat semina a Deo vero condita esse, a quo conduntur et corpora, licet cum voluptate emittantur. Semina ergo a Deo fieri confitetur, in quibus esse dicit diabolicum malum; et non erubescit credere a Deo fieri malum, quod innocentibus imputetur.
pass_a_gloss: But I wonder everywhere at the constancy of the disputant, who pronounces that seeds were founded by the true God, by whom bodies also are founded, although they are emitted with pleasure. He confesses therefore that seeds are made by God, in which he says there is a diabolical evil; and he does not blush to believe that an evil is made by God which is imputed to innocents.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Yet everywhere I marvel at our debater’s consistency. He declares that seed is created by the true God, who also creates bodies, although it is emitted with pleasure. He therefore confesses that God makes the seed in which he says diabolical evil exists. And he is not ashamed to believe that God makes an evil to be imputed to the innocent.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Seed is God's work in generation; Julian refuses to make semen a vehicle of natural evil.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
